# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 26 ADRIAN TRELEAVEN’S CONFESSION

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“I am extremely sorry that Hugh is not here,” Nell remarked. “A grave mishap befell Wace Lyons at the Glen, forcing him to leave. His return is unlikely to occur before a very late hour. Nevertheless, he instructed me that he would head up to your place sufficiently early tomorrow morning so that he could catch you prior to your departure. It is deeply frustrating. A delightful little gathering for your final evening in this place had been arranged by Tabitha and me.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0000 }

Next to the garden stream, upon the small wooden bench that Hugh had constructed, she was seated. Positioned in front of her, Adrian Treleaven leaned against the yellow birch's bronze trunk. A distinct pallor was upon him, and his face displayed the evidence of the previous night spent without sleep. Looking upward toward him, Nell pondered whether, despite everything, he had gained the vigor from his summer that it ought to have given him. Was his labor on his book excessive? It occurred to her that he had not appeared healthy for a week.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0001 }

Adrian spoke with deliberation, “Having the doctor absent makes me somewhat pleased. Mrs. Carrow, my intention was to meet with you privately. If I do not disclose something to someone, it feels as though it will push me to insanity. For seven days, I have attempted to confront it directly—yet I am unable to do so. You possess my trust, I am certain—plus, comprehension will come to you. Understanding is constant in a woman whose eyes resemble yours. You belong to those individuals who naturally draw confidences from others. Lorna is loved by me, Mrs. Carrow. LOVED! A word that faint hardly seems sufficient!”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0002 }

The restrained intensity of his speech caused his voice to crack without warning. Turning his head aside, he concealed his countenance upon his arm. His entire body trembled. Pale and horrified, Nell remained sitting as she watched him. Such a possibility had never crossed her mind! Yet—why had it never occurred to her? The situation appeared natural and unavoidable now. Her former inability to see it amazed her. Nevertheless—such occurrences were unheard of in Seven Gulls. Beyond these borders, mankind's desires might ignore societal rules and statutes—yet certainly not HERE. During a period of ten years, Lorna had occasionally taken in summer visitors, and no such event had ever transpired. Still, those guests might not have resembled Adrian Treleaven; furthermore, the vibrant, ALIVE Lorna of the present season was distinct from the distant, moody young woman of previous times. Oh, THIS ought to have been anticipated by someone! What kept Miss Winifred from foreseeing it? Miss Winifred was consistently prompt to raise a warning regarding men. An irrational anger toward Miss Winifred arose within Nell. Subsequently, she uttered a faint quiet sigh. Regardless of who bore the fault, the damage had been inflicted. And what about Lorna? Nell experienced the deepest worry on Lorna's account.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0003 }

“Is Lorna aware of this, Mr. Treleaven?” she inquired softly.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0004 }

“No—no,—provided she hasn't deduced it. You certainly cannot believe I would act as enough of a cad and scoundrel to inform her, Mrs. Carrow. I was unable to prevent myself from loving her—that is everything—and my agony exceeds what I am capable of bearing.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0005 }

“Is SHE concerned?” inquired Nell. As soon as the words were spoken, a sense that the question ought to have been withheld came over her. With an excessively enthusiastic denial, Adrian Treleaven responded to it.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0006 }

“No—no, certainly not. However, if she were available, I could cause her to feel affection—I am certain I could.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0007 }

“Though she truly cares, he is aware of it,” was the thought that crossed Nell's mind. Speaking aloud, her voice carried both empathy and firmness:
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0008 }

“Yet her freedom is absent, Mr. Treleaven. And departing quietly while abandoning her to her own existence remains the sole action available to you.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0009 }

“I understand—I understand,” Adrian uttered with a groan. Sitting on the bank of grass, he gazed gloomily down at the amber-colored water below. “I understand there is no alternative—no alternative except uttering formally, 'Good-bye, Mrs. Vane. Thank you for all your kindness to me this summer,’ in the exact manner I would have spoken it to the comely, energetic, sharp-sighted homemaker I anticipated she would be upon my arrival. After that, I will hand over my lodging fee like every truthful boarder and depart! Oh, it is quite uncomplicated. Zero doubt—zero confusion—a direct path to the edge of the earth!
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0010 }

“And I will tread it—there is no need for you to doubt that I shall, Mrs. Carrow. Yet treading on glowing hot ploughshares would be less difficult.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0011 }

The sharpness of his tone caused Nell to recoil. Little that she might utter could properly address such circumstances. Accusations were entirely improper—counsel was uncalled for—and the man’s unmitigated anguish made any condolences seem absurd. Lost in a tangle of pity and remorse, she could merely share in his grief. How her soul grieved for Lorna! Was it not true that the unfortunate young woman had already endured plenty prior to this?
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0012 }

“If she were simply happy, departing and abandoning her would not be quite so difficult,” Adrian continued with intense emotion. “However, considering her living death—comprehending the exact nature of the situation to which I am abandoning her! THAT constitutes the most terrible part of everything. I would trade my own existence to bring her happiness—yet I am powerless to even assist her—powerless. She remains tied for eternity to that miserable creature—having no prospect except aging throughout a series of vacant, purposeless, infertile years. The thought of it makes me insane. Nevertheless, I have to live out my existence, never beholding her, yet perpetually aware of what she suffers. It is ghastly—ghastly!”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0013 }

“It is extremely difficult,” Nell said with grief. “We—those of us who are her friends here—are all aware of how difficult it is for her.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0014 }

“And she possesses such abundant gifts for living,” Adrian stated in a tone of defiance.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0015 }

“Her attractiveness represents the smallest part of her inheritance—and she is the most gorgeous female I have ever encountered. That chuckling sound she makes! I have spent the entire summer scheming to bring forth that chuckle, merely for the joy of listening to it. And her gaze—it possesses a depth and blue hue matching the gulf yonder. I have not witnessed such azure before—and gilded shades! Have you ever observed her tresses loose, Mrs. Carrow?”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0016 }

“No.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0017 }

“I did—on one occasion. I had traveled down to the Point aiming to go fishing with Captain Saul, but the water was too rough for us to head out, which caused me to return. Taking advantage of an afternoon she assumed she would spend by herself, she had washed her hair and was standing outdoors on the veranda drying it in the sunlight. It cascaded clear down to her feet around her like a fountain of living gold. Spotting me, she rushed indoors, as the wind seized her hair and swept it all about her—resembling Danae in her cloud. Somehow, right at that instance, the awareness that I loved her struck me—and I understood that I had been in love with her since the very first moment I beheld her against the darkness in that radiant glow. And now she is forced to remain here—tending to and comforting Rufus, skimping and economizing simply to survive, while I pass my days in futile longing for her, prevented, by that exact circumstance, from providing her even the slight assistance a friend could offer. I paced the beach last night, nearly until daybreak, wrestling with the entire situation again and again. Even so, despite all of this, I am unable to bring myself to regret coming to Seven Gulls. To my mind, as awful as the situation stands, it would prove far worse had I never met Lorna. Loving her and parting from her causes a scorching, searing agony—yet never having loved her remains completely unimaginable. I imagine all of this strikes you as quite mad—these overwhelming feelings always appear absurd whenever we express them through our imperfect language. They were never intended to be voiced—merely experienced and borne. I ought not to have said anything—yet it has provided some relief. At the very least, it has supplied me with the fortitude to depart in a proper manner tomorrow morning, without causing a disturbance. You will send me letters occasionally, will you not, Mrs. Carrow, and share whatever updates there are concerning her?”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0018 }

“Indeed,” Nell remarked. “Ah, I am deeply grieved that you are leaving—we shall miss you greatly—we have all been such good companions! Were it not because of this, you might return during future summers. Maybe, even now—eventually—once you have put it out of your mind, maybe—”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0019 }

“Seven Gulls will never see me again, nor will the memory ever leave me,” Adrian stated succinctly.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0020 }

Quietness and dusk descended upon the garden. Off in the distance, the ocean was beating softly and repetitively against the bar. The night breeze among the poplars made a noise similar to a melancholy, strange, ancient chant—a fragmented vision of former recollections. A slim, well-formed young aspen stood in front of them against the delicate yellow-orange, green, and fading pink of the western sky, a backdrop that revealed each leaf and twig in dark, quivering, magical beauty.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0021 }

“Is that not lovely?” Adrian asked, gesturing toward it like someone who is setting a particular discussion aside.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0022 }

“Because of its intense beauty, I feel a physical pain,” Nell uttered in a quiet voice. “Flawless objects such as this have constantly caused me distress—I can recall terming the sensation ‘the queer ache’ during my youth. Why does an agony of this nature appear to be inextricably linked to absolute flawlessness? Does it stem from the sorrow of absolute completion—the moment it dawns on us that any subsequent change can only be a decline?”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0023 }

“It may be,” Adrian said in a dreamy voice, “that our own captive endlessness is crying out to the matching endlessness displayed by that seen flawlessness.”
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0024 }

“It appears you are suffering from a head cold. It would be wise to apply some tallow to your nose before sleeping,” remarked Miss Winifred, having entered via the small gate among the fir trees just as Adrian finished speaking. Although Adrian was well-liked by Miss Winifred, she made it a point of principle to penalize any grandiloquent speech coming from a gentleman with a snub nose.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0025 }

Miss Winifred embodied the humor that constantly lurks behind the tragic aspects of existence. Having experienced somewhat frayed nerves, Nell chuckled uncontrollably, and Adrian offered a smile as well. Indeed, emotional intensity and romance tended to retreat into the background whenever Miss Winifred was around. Even so, the situation no longer appeared entirely as bleak, gloomy, and distressing to Nell as it had just a short time earlier. Nevertheless, rest remained completely elusive to her during those nocturnal hours.
{: #nw-v04-c26-p0026 }
